newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Astra to export cars in ASEAN by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Astra to export cars in ASEAN by 1998.

text.p: Astra International's unit PT Toyota Astra Motor plans to start exporting its popular multi-purpose Kijang vehicle to ASEAN countries from 1998, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Thursday.
Rudyanto Hardjanto, president-director of Toyota Astra Motor, said 2,500 to 3,000 vehicles would be exported in a completely knocked down form per month.
"We will start the exports next year with ASEAN countries as our first priority," Hardjanto was quoted as saying.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore and Vietnam.
Hardjanto said Astra planned to allocate a quarter of its 1998 production target of 100,000 vehicles to the overseas market.
He said the company needed additional investment of at least 300 billion rupiah to meet a 60 percent of local content target for its car.
"Currently, local content in the new-model of Kijang is 45 percent, up from 43.6 percent in 1995," he said.
In order to meet the 60 percent local content requirement, he said, the company planned to establish a components plant to make transmissions and rear axles.
"Plans to establish a component plant should be finalised this year, so by 1999 we can achieve the target of 60 percent local contents," he added.

Minister for Industry and Trade Tungky Ariwibowo announced on February 28 last year that car makers wholly owned by Indonesians, who used Indonesian technology and met local content requirements, would get tax and tariff breaks.
